item.title: Democrats win Texas governor and Senate races for first time in decades
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Democrat James Talarico defeated the state’s attorney general Ken Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump who survived impeachment and years of scandal (ALEX WONG) Democrat James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminarian who campaigned on a “politics of love,” on Tuesday won the US Senate race in Texas, dealing a historic blow to Republicans that could reshape American politics. Talarico defeated the state's attorney general Ken Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump who survived impeachment and years of scandal, US media projected. The result was a major setback for Trump, who threw his weight behind Paxton and made the state a campaign priority. In another political earthquake for the deeply conservative southern border state, Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseated incumbent Texas Governor Greg Abbott. Talarico and Hinojosa are the first Democrats to win statewide office in Texas since 1994. Hinojosa, a 52-year-old attorney and state lawmaker, is part of a new generation of Democrats who are seeking to attract independents and voters disillusioned by Trump’s unpopular war in the Middle East and skyrocketing prices for gas and everyday goods. Thousands of supporters gathered at a watch party in Austin erupted in joy as the results came in, many of them crying and hugging. Some chanted "Si se puede" ("Yes we can" in Spanish), while drivers passing by honked their horns in celebration. "It's a huge win for Texas, but it’s a giant win for the United States, having James Talarico in the Senate to try to wrest control of this government that's out of control," said Kathy Jackoway, an Austin resident in her 60s, who shouted and cried when the results were announced. "Everybody is suffering. Everybody is hurting, and Trump is busy building monuments to himself." Anisha, 29, said she hoped the two Democrats would govern "for everyone, not just the billionaires, not just the elite." The landmark victories for Democrats could signal that Texas, the country’s second most populous state with 40 electoral votes, is becoming competitive in national elections, a shift that could reshape the electoral map for future races. The results mark a bruising defeat for tech multi-billionaire Elon Musk, who spent more than $200 million to support Talarico's rival, according to federal filings. The world's richest man, Musk has moved the headquarters of Tesla, SpaceX and X to Texas, and has a growing business stake in the state. - 'Uniting Texans' - The spread of AI data centers across Texas became a central issue in both races, as residents worry about rising electricity bills, water use and strain on the power grid. Talarico and Hinojosa both called for tighter regulation, prompting Abbott, a longtime champion of the industry, to propose new rules of his own. Talarico ran on a blend of Christian faith and economic populism, describing the contest as a David versus Goliath fight and inviting Republicans dissatisfied with the party to join him. "We are uniting Texans from all backgrounds and beliefs onto one team to take on this broken, corrupt political system," he told reporters after voting early in Austin last week. Trump traveled to Texas four times in the month before the election to rally for Paxton, whom he endorsed over four-term incumbent senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary. Talarico, a 37-year-old former teacher and Presbyterian seminarian, was elected to the Texas House of Representatives in 2018 and built a national following with speeches combining progressive politics, biblical teaching and criticism of wealthy elites. He defeated congresswoman Jasmine Crockett in the Democratic primary and sought to broaden his appeal by criticizing aspects of former president Joe Biden’s immigration policies. Paxton, 63, survived impeachment by the Republican-controlled Texas House in 2023 on allegations of corruption and abuse of power before being acquitted by the state Senate. He has denied wrongdoing. During the campaign, Talarico drew support from voters who had left the Republican Party and younger voters. bur-arp/sla This article originally appeared on AFP at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/talarico-flips-texas-senate-seat-042452269.html

item.title: Trump says U.S. is ready to strike Iran as negotiators struggle to reach deal
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
By Parisa Hafezi and Jana Choukeir DUBAI, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Iran and the United States are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, as US President Donald Trump declined to rule out a resumption of US combat operations after the elections in the United States. Trump made his comments in separate interviews as Americans voted in ‌pivotal midterm elections in which the unpopular Iran war has been a key factor and as mediator Qatar stepped up efforts to avert a renewed escalation. Overnight, the United States carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's ‌Qeshm island, targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations. Trump on Tuesday renewed warnings of military action in an interview with the Fox News Channel. "I'm not looking ​to ... kill lots of people," he said. "If we have to, we'll have to." In an interview with the Financial Times, Trump suggested he was content with the state of the stand-off with Iran. "We seem to be getting everything we want," the paper quoted him as saying in a six-minute telephone interview. The FT said it asked Trump about what it called "strong hints" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that there would be an attack later this week. "I’m ready, we’re ready. We’re locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," he replied. Trump told the FT indirect negotiations with Iran about its stockpile of enriched uranium were ongoing. "We’re having discussions, and we’ll see how that all works out," ‌he said. Also on Tuesday, Trump made a surprise announcement of a deal with ⁠Netanyahu under which Washington would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after this year, but would sell weapons to its close Middle East ally. The remarks appeared aimed at swaying voters unhappy with US support for Israel. Fears have grown that the conflict launched by the United States and Israel in February could flare up again after Tuesday's midterms. "Mediators are ⁠working hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington," the senior Iranian official said, speaking on condition of anonymity. Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night for talks on a version of a draft US-Iran deal discussed over the past eight days. "Tehran's conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened," the Iranian official cautioned, referring to Iranian demands including waiving oil sanctions, ending the US naval blockade and releasing frozen Iranian funds. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, later said ​the ​US response to Iranian demands "was not convincing", adding that Washington "must fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions and act upon them". "Only ​in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened," he wrote on X. 'WE CANNOT ‌LOSE HOPE' Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said both the United States and Iran were reviewing proposals put forward by mediators. While the Qatari team that travelled to Tehran had returned to Doha, talks were continuing. "There are intensive joint regional efforts underway to avoid escalation," he told a news briefing, adding that Qatar remained hopeful a deal could still be reached to pave the way for future negotiations. "If there were no glimmer of hope, there would be no negotiations... and as a mediator, we cannot lose hope," he said. An official briefed on the talks said feedback from Washington and Tehran was expected within the next 36 hours. A senior Iranian official told Reuters later on Tuesday that there is no deadline for exchanging messages with Washington through mediators or reviewing responses. 'FORCEFUL RESPONSE' The senior Iranian official said Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands" and that nuclear talks could begin only after Iran's conditions were met. Tehran would respond ‌forcefully, in the region and beyond, to US strikes, the official added. Oil prices slipped in early trade on Wednesday as investors ​awaited the results of the midterm elections and their potential impact on peace talks, even after industry data showed US crude stocks unexpectedly ​fell last week. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said the ball was in Washington's court after a "strong ​and rational response" from Tehran. "The enemy seeks to force the Iranian nation into submission through threats and military action, but they are sorely mistaken; Iran will not submit," Qalibaf said. ‌He said Tehran's response to any US miscalculation would be unpredictable and unconstrained by ​geography. The head of Iran's armed forces general staff, Ali Abdollahi, ​said Iran's military was updating target lists that included US and Israeli assets and would respond immediately to any threat. Hardline newspaper Kayhan said on Tuesday that US facilities in Britain, Italy, Greece, Romania, Albania and Cyprus could be targeted in the event of renewed war. IRANIAN-SAUDI TALKS Alongside indirect exchanges between Tehran and Washington, regional powers are pursuing diplomatic efforts to prevent further escalation. The conflict has also widened, with Yemen's Iran-aligned ​Houthis stepping up attacks on Saudi Arabia. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Tuesday ‌talks with Saudi Arabia were continuing to seek new regional security arrangements that would exclude foreign military involvement. Last week, senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian counterparts in Tehran, ​the first such high-level contacts since August. (Additional reporting by Nayera Abdallah, Tala Ramadan and Elwely Elwelly in Dubai, Andrew Mills in Doha, Doina Chiacu and David Brunnstrom in Washington, Yasmine Ghania in ​Cairo; Writing by Dubai Newsroom and Tom Perry, Editing by Raju Gopalakrishnan, Ros Russell, Don Durfee and Kate Mayberry) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://uk.news.yahoo.com/irans-foreign-minister-says-talks-071254829.html

item.title: Trump says U.S. will halt $4 billion in annual aid to Israel and shift to selling arms
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
President Donald Trump declared Tuesday that the U.S. will end nearly $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel, an unusually timed announcement on Election Day that could set up a standoff with Congress. The president said on "Fox and Friends" that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed "months ago" to stop the aid by the end of the year. "They're fine with it because they've become a very successful country," Trump said. "They don't need it. And we won't be paying anymore...we won't be paying Israel. We'll help Israel if they need it. They've been a great ally." The announcement could portend a significant shift in the U.S.-Israel relationship, which has long been underpinned by billions of dollars in American military assistance. Under a 10-year agreement signed during the Obama administration, the U.S. committed to providing Israel with $38 billion in military aid between 2019 and 2028. The earlier time frame raises questions about how the administration intends to suddenly halt the assistance, and whether Congress would need to approve the change. More than 90 percent of the money is directed to American defense companies, essentially never leaving the U.S. The Pentagon referred questions to the White House, which did not respond to a request for comment. The Israeli embassy could not be reached for comment. Trump, in the interview on Tuesday morning, said the annual assistance to Israel is a "bad talking point" for Democrats, including Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. "The left uses the $4 billion payment … as a signal of unfairness. And we can't allow that to happen. I don't like that. … It's almost too easy to target." Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-Ga.), who unsuccessfully pushed to cut military assistance to Israel while in Congress, suggested the announcement was motivated by Republicans' political troubles ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections. "Amazing how being on the verge of Republicans getting wiped out in the midterms changes hearts and minds," Greene wrote on social media. "Trump getting permission from Netanyahu to end annual aid to Israel isn't going to change today's election results. But it does show you how bad the polling is on that issue." The announcement also comes just a week after Israel's parliamentary elections left Netanyahu fighting to hold onto power. His Likud party emerged with the most seats, but his right-wing coalition fell short of the 61 seats needed for a majority, teeing up difficult negotiations to form a new government. Israel's standing in the United States has eroded over the past three years amid public outrage over the country's actions in the Gaza war. Many Democrats increasingly favor conditioning if not outright ending U.S military aid to Israel. A growing number of Republicans, eager to reduce U.S. military interventions abroad, see Israel as an obstacle to that goal. Israel is categorized as a major non-NATO ally, a designation which prioritizes it for arms sales and transfers of excess American military equipment. The vast majority of the military funding comes in the form of financing that allows Israel to buy U.S. military equipment. It traditionally includes $3.3 billion in foreign military financing and another $500 million for cooperative missile defense programs. The funding counts for less than one percent of the annual U.S. federal budget. Netanyahu has hinted for years that Israel will have to become more independent of U.S. military financing. He told CBS News earlier this year that he wanted to reduce U.S. support to zero. Trump insisted the Israeli leader first broached the topic. Netanyahu said, '"It would be appropriate if we don't receive aid,' because he understands that this is one of their points of contention." But Netanyahu is also keen to maintain U.S.-Israeli defense cooperation, especially on technology. Some in Israeli and American circles want to push for more such partnerships. This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/trump-says-end-billions-dollars-152022589.html

item.title: 'I wasn't on the ballot': Trump distances himself from GOP midterm losses
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
President Donald Trump sought to distance himself from Republicans' mounting midterm losses Tuesday, declaring in his first remarks on the election results that his party would have been victorious had he been on the ballot. "I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" Trump wrote on social media. Trump's efforts to sidestep blame for the growing blue wave came as Republicans were dealt stunning losses in deep red states and districts, with Democrats flipping Senate seats in Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Ohio. Republicans also lost Senate races in North Carolina and Georgia, and are trailing in other key contests. Trump told the New York Times that he is "absolutely willing to accept" the election results. “We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out," Trump said. Democrats are poised to flip both chambers of Congress by wide margins, with the party seizing on backlash to Trump's second-term agenda, including concerns about his handling of the economy and the Iran war. Despite his record-low approval rating, Trump thrust himself into the center of the midterm election with a series of rallies across 20 states in the closing weeks. The midterm contests are shaping up to be an emphatic repudiation of a president who implored voters to "pretend" he was on the ballot. item.title: Democrat Amy Acton wins Ohio governor's race, ending 20-year GOP streak
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Dr. Amy Acton speaks at a campaign rally in Toledo, Ohio, on Oct. 29, 2026. —Michael M. Santiago—Getty Images Dr. Amy Acton will be Ohio’s next governor, defeating her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy in a heated race that has gained national attention in recent weeks over a controversial attack-ad against the Democrat. On Tuesday evening, AP called the race for Acton, who previously served as the director of the state’s health department during the COVID-19 pandemic, reporting that she won 50.8% of the vote with 86% of votes counted. Ramaswamy, who was backed by President Donald Trump, earned 45.9% of the vote, according to AP. Acton’s victory marks the first time in two decades that Ohioans have elected a Democrat to the governorship. It represents a significant blow to Republicans, who initially liked their chances in a state that the President won by double digits in the 2024 election. Ramaswamy attack ad sparks widespread controversy The race, which was an open battle since current Republican Gov. Mike DeWine was restricted from running again because of term limits, took a striking turn in the lead-up to Election Day. The Cook Political Report had previously rated the race as “Lean Republican,” but later adjusted its analysis and marked it a “Toss Up.” On Oct. 23, though, the Cook Political Report shifted the race slightly in Democrats’ favor to “Lean Democrat.” The election forecaster attributed its latest assessment in part to an attack ad released by Ramaswamy’s campaign in October. The ad featured Acton’s estranged mother, who lost custody of Acton and her brother in 1978, the same year that their stepfather was indicted on charges of raping Acton when she was a child. It sparked backlash across the political aisle. Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, described the ad as “a despicable low.” “It’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” Stearns said in a statement . “This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core—a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants.” The state’s current Republican governor said that the ad was “deeply, deeply troubling” and “just plain wrong,” calling for Ramaswamy’s campaign to rescind it. DeWine maintained, nonetheless, that he still endorsed Ramaswamy and “the whole [Republican] ticket.” But Ramaswamy, who launched an unsuccessful bid for the Republican nomination in the 2024 election, doubled down on the ad. Both Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance defended him in the wake of the outrage. This article originally appeared on Time at https://time.com/article/2026/11/04/amy-acton-ohio-governor-ramaswamy-midterm-election-bitter-race-against/

item.title: Democrats on track for full control of Congress after flipping Senate
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Democrats have regained control of the U.S. Senate, winning races in several key states, and appear poised to win back the House as Republican midterm losses mount. In Georgia, Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff won reelection, easily defeating his Republican challenger, Rep. Mike Collins. In North Carolina, Democrat Roy Cooper defeated Republican Michael Whatley to flip a Senate seat there. In South Carolina, Democrat Annie Andrews beat GOP Sen. Darline Graham to flip another. In Ohio, former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown defeated incumbent GOP Sen. Jon Husted, another flip. In Texas, James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton, becoming the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate seat in the Lone Star State since 1988. And in Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson defeated incumbent GOP Sen. Susan Collins, putting an end to her three-decade tenure. Coming into the night, Republicans held 53 of the Senate’s 100 seats, compared with 45 held by Democrats. There are two independents — Sens. Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Angus King of Maine — who caucus with the Democrats. To wrest back control of the Senate, Democrats needed a net gain of at least four seats. Before the clock struck midnight on the East Coast, the Associated Press said the party would gain at least that amount — with several other key races still to be decided. In the 435-seat House, the GOP held 218 seats, compared with 214 held by Democrats. To retake control of the House , Democrats needed a net gain of three seats — and early returns suggest they are on their way to exceeding that figure. There are also 36 gubernatorial races and numerous ballot measures to keep an eye on. On Tuesday, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history, while Democrat Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds became the state’s first Black governor-elect. President Trump, whose approval ratings are at or near all-time lows, spent the last month campaigning in battleground states, urging voters to "pretend" he was on the ballot to encourage higher turnout in hopes that it would help Republicans avert a so-called blue wave . In a post on Truth Social on Tuesday night, Trump distanced himself from mounting Republican losses. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump wrote. “Thank you for your attention to this matter.” This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/live/midterms-2026-live-updates-election-day-voters-head-to-the-polls-as-democrats-look-to-flip-gop-control-of-the-house-and-senate-110000715.html

item.title: A rare condition killed a 24-year-old first-time NYC Marathon runner. Its warning signs can be easy to miss.
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Just two miles short of the finish line of the 2026 New York City Marathon on Nov. 1, 24-year-old runner Rachel Apa collapsed. She died of a rare and potentially life-threatening illness that can be brought on by excessive exertion, the New York Times reported. It's called rhabdomyolysis , and while there are relatively few cases nationwide each year, it can strike during endurance or intensive exercise, including marathons. What happened to Rachel Apa? Apa was running her first marathon to raise money for Parkinson's disease in honor of her late grandfather, according to the New York Times. But Apa was no stranger to athletics, having played Division I field hockey in college. Her family said Apa had been in "perfect health." Plus, she'd been training for the race for months. But at mile 18, Apa texted her father, Steve, who'd been checking in at each mile: "Ow." At the end of the next mile, she wrote, "Ow ow." She stopped responding after that. Apa's mother, Michelle, was at the race and had watched her daughter run by earlier on. Her parents noticed on the marathon tracking app that Apa stopped moving after mile 24. Apa collapsed just after running past hospital social worker Michaela Nichols, who was cheering on participants. Nichols ran over and checked Apa's pulse, but couldn't find one. Three other people — two of whom said they were physicians — ran over to give Apa CPR. Marathon medical staff tried to revive her with a defibrillator before an ambulance arrived. She was taken to Mount Sinai Medical Center and treated for six hours, but could not be saved. Her father told the New York Times that Apa's cause of death was rhabdomyolysis. What is rhabdomyolysis? It's a dangerous medical condition that occurs when skeletal muscle (the kind that connects to bones and allows you to move) gets damaged and rapidly breaks down. "The internal components of muscle cells, which include various electrolytes, proteins and enzymes, spill out, and those in turn can be toxic to the kidneys and dangerous to the heart," Dr. David Mariuma , a nephrologist at Stony Brook Medicine who was not involved in Apa's treatment, tells Yahoo. Specifically, the released molecules can lead to kidney failure and life-threatening heart arrhythmias if not treated quickly and properly. This destructive process can be triggered in several different ways. The most common cause is not exercise, but injury, according to the Cleveland Clinic. Traumatic crushing injuries are the most likely to induce rhabdomyolysis (often referred to as simply "rhabdo"), but severe burns or electrocution can also lead to muscle breakdown. Cleveland Clinic reports that there are about 26,000 total cases of rhabdomyolysis in the U.S. each year. It's harder to say exactly how many are due to exercise, but one study estimates that physical exertion — including endurance athletic activities, manual labor and intense exercise — may account for up to 47% of cases. The true number is likely higher, Mariuma says. Who is at risk? Although it's uncommon, anyone can develop rhabdomyolysis, regardless of age and athletic experience. Dr. Jessica Tomazic , a sports and exercise medicine staff physician with the Cleveland Clinic who was not involved in Apa's care nor familiar with her case, tells Yahoo that a combination of risk factors can increase the likelihood. They include: Dehydration Heat, or temperatures one is not accustomed to exercising in Being sick Certain genetic conditions, including sickle cell disease Recent consumption of alcohol Drug use (particularly cocaine, according to Mariuma) Prior heat illness, rhabdomyolysis or a family history of rhabdo Rhabdomyolysis is also more common among men, people who smoke and those with obesity. In rare cases, certain medications, including statins, can lead to the condition when the dose is too high for an individual patient, says Mariuma. Higher rates of rhabdomyolysis have also been linked to endurance athletes, spin classes and high-intensity interval training, including the P90X workout program. And researchers have looked specifically at cases of rhabdo among New York City marathon runners. An Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai study identified at least one rhabdo incident each year between 2017 and 2024 (excluding 2020, when the marathon was canceled due to COVID). Twenty-one-year-old Austin Stallman died of rhabdomyolysis after collapsing during a 9-mile Navy SEAL training run in Texas earlier in 2026. "This is the kind of thing where sometimes everything could go right, you could do everything you're supposed to do and it still happens," says Mariuma. What are the symptoms? The condition can be hard to spot because many of its symptoms are similar to what some people experience during intense physical challenges. It typically begins with soreness or pain that feels more extreme than usual for the activity, according to Mariuma and Tomiazic. Pain is especially concerning if it's accompanied by more weakness than normal or "any sense of confusion, nausea, or what we call constitutional symptoms that are not specific to the muscle — a general sense that something is off, or malaise," says Mariuma. Another telltale sign is dark urine, the color of tea or soda, he adds. But a marathon runner is unlikely to detect this signal mid-race. How to prevent rhabdomyolysis — and what to do if it happens Gradually training for a new activity, rather than jumping in at full tilt, can help reduce the risk. It's also important to stay hydrated not only during but also leading up to and after an activity that requires a lot of exertion, both experts advise. And if you're feeling at all unwell, stay home or at least keep your physical activity light, as intense activity while sick is a risk factor for the condition. Tomazic, who is also a trail runner and ski patroller, acknowledges that the symptoms and risk factors — such as not properly fueling with water and food — can be easy to lose track of, especially mid-competition. "We — I say we because I do these things — we tend to push through pain; that's the mindset that we're encouraged to take," Tomazic says. "So sometimes it can be difficult to determine, 'Is this a pain that I should really listen to, or is it a pain that I can monitor, for now?'" If you notice any symptoms of rhabdomyolysis, acting quickly is important, especially if you have risk factors for the condition, because "when it happens, it tends to happen over minutes to hours," says Mariuma. You should stop what you're doing, call for help and try to find some shade if you're outside on a hot day, Tomazic says. Staying well hydrated helps dilute and flush out myoglobin, the muscle protein that can build up during rhabdomyolysis, and other molecules. But he adds, don't overdo it on plain water. Make sure you're getting electrolytes from your diet or sports drinks during intense athletic activities, since too much water without them can cause a dangerous condition called hyponatremia . Rhabdomyolysis is primarily treated with IV fluids, which help the kidneys clear myoglobin and other substances released from damaged muscles. In cases where the kidneys have already suffered damage, some patients may receive dialysis, according to the Cleveland Clinic. More than 90% of patients who don't develop kidney damage from rhabdo survive, but the fatality rate rises to more than 20% with kidney injury, according to one study. But overall, both Tomazic and Mariuma say that rhabdo shouldn't discourage you from running or participating in the physical activities you want to do. "Exercise-related rhabdo is rare … so I wouldn't use a tragedy like this as a reason to not do a marathon," says Mariuma. "Any activity out there, there are risks, and the only thing we can really do is learn the best ways to prevent them." item.title: Tennessee murderer captured in Missouri after prison escape and truck theft
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Authorities have captured a convicted murderer who evaded law enforcement for more than a week after escaping from a Tennessee prison. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation announced Tuesday that Jacob Morley was back in custody. He was arrested near Kansas City, Missouri, investigators said. "Thank you to the public for your assistance, vigilance, and the tips provided during this investigation," the bureau said in a statement. "We also thank all of our law enforcement partners for their continued efforts to safely bring this search to a successful conclusion." Investigators got a tip Tuesday morning that Morley had been hiding in a shed at a hunting camp around Marion, Illinois, some 320 miles south of Chicago, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said in a statement. Authorities also learned a truck had been stolen from the property. Missouri State Highway Patrol said it handled Morley's arrest alongside multiple partner agencies, after Tennessee authorities reported that Morley may be traveling through Missouri, based on footage obtained through Flock cameras. The arrest happened around 11:30 a.m. local time near Norborne, a small city about an hour's drive from Kansas City, the state agency said. Authorities said they also recovered three firearms that had previously been reported stolen inside the truck. Little information about the inmate's escape and the multi-state search for him has been made available since Morley broke out of prison. But investigators said more will be released as it becomes available. Morley, 28, was serving a life sentence at the Northwest Correctional Complex in an isolated part of Tiptonville, a town roughly 90 miles from Memphis in northwestern Tennessee. He had been convicted of killing a coworker four years ago, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. Correctional officers discovered Morley was missing from the prison at around 11:30 p.m. local time on Oct. 25, the department said. While parsing security cameras later on, investigators said they saw footage of Morley escaping the complex while wearing his prison uniform by slipping through a fence on the property. Authorities released additional security footage two days later that showed the inmate stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350, with Tennessee plates and a logo for Lindamood Planting Company on the side door, in the early hours of Oct. 27. It was stolen from Lake County, which includes Tiptonville, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said. The truck was located later the same day in Marion, Illinois, which is about 150 miles north of Tiptonville, the investigative bureau said . Morley's whereabouts were unknown at the time. The bureau had said earlier in the week that Morley was on its "most wanted" list, as various agencies, including the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, the governor's office and U.S. Marshals, offered combined rewards of up to $17,500 for information leading to his arrest. Investigators haven't shared details about how exactly the inmate escaped, beyond the fact that he breached a fence at the prison. Morley received a lifetime prison sentence for murdering Cody Birchfield, his former coworker, in 2022. Authorities said Birchfield's body was found in a box under Morley's home in Tennessee's Carter County after he had been missing for several weeks. In addition to first-degree murder, Morley was convicted of aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, vandalism and evading arrest, as he fled when deputies arrived at his home in 2022. Authorities said the manhunt for him at the time ended in North Carolina. Northwest Correctional Complex is a men's prison with the capacity to hold 1,776 inmates under varying degrees of security, from the lowest level up to maximum, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. It also houses minors who have been convicted of crimes as adults. Multiple violent incidents have taken place inside the prison in recent years, some of which involved attacks between inmates and prison staff. In July, a grand jury returned dozens of indictments over the murders of five inmates, assaults against staff and other acts of violence. At a recent meeting of the Tennessee Inmate Disciplinary Oversight Board, members discussed ongoing problems in the prison and suggested issues with leadership played a role. item.title: At least 124 people shot nationwide over Halloween weekend
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Violence at parties and other festivities marred the Halloween weekend, as police in multiple cities across the country investigated shootings and other mayhem that left at least 124 people shot, 17 fatally, authorities said. "This is not normal," Delaware Gov. Matt Meyers said after shootings erupted at Halloween events in two cities in his state over the weekend. "We must never accept gun violence as part of life in Delaware." KXTV - PHOTO: In this screen grab from a video, first responders are shown at the scene of a shooting at a Spirit Halloween store inside the Solano Town Center in Fairfield, Calif., on Oct. 30, 2026. Shootings occurred over the weekend at Halloween house parties and street parties in at least 15 cities, from California to Delaware, and the victims included a 5-year-old girl still in her Halloween costume, a pregnant woman and a college student, according to law enforcement officials. One shooting even occurred at a Halloween supply store. 15 shot, three fatally, in Chicago over Halloween weekend The Chicago Police Department said officers responded to multiple shootings that left 15 people shot, three fatally. Police said the victims who were killed included a 35-year-old man who was shot during an argument in the Mayfair neighborhood. One person of interest was taken into custody, police told ABC Chicago station WLS. A 29-year-old man was killed and three others were shot in the North Lawndale neighborhood, when a two gunman exited a car and opened fire as the victims stood on a sidewalk. A 41-year-old man died early Sunday after being shot and transporting himself to Holy Cross Hospital. No further information was released on the shooting. 2 shootings in Delaware leave girl dead and 8 other people wounded The two shootings in Delaware happened on Saturday, Halloween night. One occurred at an outdoor Halloween party in Ellendale and left a 17-year-old girl dead and eight others wounded, according to the Ellendale Police Department. "During an outdoor party, an unknown suspect allegedly opened fire from a neighboring property into a crowd, striking nine people," according to police. No arrests have been announced. The other shooting in Delaware occurred in Newark near the University of Delaware and left six people suffering from gunshot wounds, according to the Newark Police Department. The shooting occurred on a sidewalk on East Main Street around 11:13 p.m. local time as hundreds of Halloween revelers were in the area. Video obtained by ABC Philadelphia station WPVI showed people suddenly running for cover as the chaos unfolded. One of the victims, a 20-year-old University of Delaware student, was hospitalized in serious condition with a bullet wound to the back and a collapsed lung, police said. A 16-year-old boy who was wounded in the gunfire was arrested after police found he had a loaded firearm, authorities said. The shooting prompted the University of Delaware to cancel classes on Monday and provide counseling to students traumatized by the incident, according to a university spokesperson. 1 dead, 6 injured in shooting at California Halloween store A day before Halloween, a shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, California, left one person dead and six others injured, police said. The shooting, which occurred around 8:30 p.m. local time, is believed to have stemmed from a targeted incident involving one suspect inside the Spirit Halloween store, police said in a statement Saturday. KXTV - PHOTO: In this screen grab from a video, first responders are shown at the scene of a shooting at a Spirit Halloween store inside the Solano Town Center in Fairfield, Calif., on Oct. 30, 2026. The person killed was identified as Constance Hages, 31, who was pregnant at the time of her death, family members told police. A 16-year-old boy, a 19-year-old man and a 32-year-old man were critically injured in the shooting, according to police. Three other men, ranging in age from 19 to 43, were also wounded in the incident, police said. At a news conference on Monday afternoon, Fairfield police announced they had arrested a suspect in the shooting. 4 fatally shot in Dallas, 15 others injured in separate shootings Dallas Police Chief Daniel Comeaux said three separate shootings occurred on Halloween night in the city's bustling Deep Ellum entertainment district. Comeaux said four people were killed and 15 others were injured in the shootings despite beefed-up patrols in the neighborhood due to it being Halloween. WFAA - PHOTO: Dallas, Texas, police investigate one of three separate shootings in the city's Deep Ellum entertainment district on Halloween, October 31, 2026, that left four people dead and 15 others injured. "This is completely unacceptable for this to take place in Dallas, and we're going to do everything we need to do to get everyone in custody who is responsible for this," Comeaux said during a news conference on Sunday. He said officers were just two blocks away and heard the gunshots when the first shooting broke out. He said one suspect is in custody as police work to find other assailants involved in the shootings. 7 shot at birthday party on Halloween in Edinburg, Texas Seven people were hospitalized in shootings that happened at a birthday party on Halloween near Edinburg, Texas, the Hildalgo County Sheriff's Office told ABC affiliate station KRGC in Weslasco, Texas. The shooting occurred around 11:45 p.m. at a home, police said. "Upon arrival, deputies determined that an adult birthday party was taking place at the location," the sheriff’s office said in a statement. "Deputies located seven victims who had sustained gunshot wounds. The victims’ injuries were determined to be non-life-threatening." 5-year-old in Halloween costume shot in Detroit Detroit police said they are investigating a shooting on Halloween night that left a 5-year-old girl, who was still in her Halloween costume, with a bullet wound to the chest. The child was playing in a back room of her house after going trick-or-treating when she was struck by a gunshot fired from outside. "For our victim, she was in her Halloween costume at the time she got shot," Detroit Deputy Police Chief Arnold Williams said during a news conference Saturday night. Arnold said the child, who is in stable condition, cried out for her mother when she was shot. "She had to tell her mom. She said, 'I think I've been shot.' The mom was in the shower and had to come down and rush her child here. This is just something senseless," Arnold said. No arrests have been announced. The incident marked the second shooting on Halloween in Michigan. In Flint, Michigan, a woman was killed and three other people were injured when gunfire broke out at a Halloween house party, according to the Flint Police Department. Two juveniles and one adult were wounded in the shooting, police said. No arrests have been made and a $2,500 reward is being offered in the case. 'Senseless': 7 shot at Halloween street celebration in Fayetteville Gunfire erupted at a Halloween celebration in an entertainment district of Fayetteville, Arkansas, on Saturday night that left seven people shot, according to the Fayetteville Police Department. In a statement, police described the shooting as a "random act of violence. Fayetteville Mayor Molly Rawn said the shooting occurred near the Dickson Street entertainment district where up to 30,000 people were out celebrating Halloween. "It was a senseless act of violence," Rawn said in a social media statement. No arrests have been announced in the incident. 2 killed in Oklahoma City shooting at Halloween night get-together In Oklahoma City, two people are killed and two others was injured after a shooting and vehicle crash involving pedestrians on Halloween night, according to the police. "Responding officers found a chaotic scene that involved two deceased people under a car, and another lying near the scene with numerous gunshot wounds," the Oklahoma City Police Department said in a statement. Investigators determined that all four victims were at a Halloween party when a fight broke out in a parking lot. Police said two men shot each other during the fight. A 20-year-old woman, identified as Kyla Hysell, allegedly got into her car and "drove into the melee," hitting two people, who were both pronounced dead at the scene, police said. Police identified the two people killed in the incident as Mayrah Torres and Isaac Lujan-Ochoa. Police said Torres and Lujan-Ochoa were both allegedly run over by Hysell and that Lujan-Ochoa was already deceased from the earlier shooting, according to police. The man who was allegedly shot in the gunfight with Lujan-Ochoa was hospitalized in critical condition, police said. Hysell was arrested on charges of aggravated driving under the influence and felony murder, police said. 1 killed, 8 wounded in shooting after football game One person was killed, and eight others were injured in a shooting after a football game in Birmingham, Alabama, on Halloween, law enforcement officials said. Will McLelland/AL.com via AP - PHOTO: Weekend Violence At least one person was detained in connection with the shooting, according to the Birmingham Police Department. Shortly after 7:50 p.m., multiple shots rang out near Legion Field, which earlier had hosted the Magic City Classic football game between Alabama A&M and Alabama State, according to police. 11 people shot in Jacksonville, Florida, 2 fatally, at Halloween events In Jacksonville, Florida, police said 11 people were shot, two fatally, in separate incidents over the Halloween weekend. A 17-year-old girl died after being shot while waiting to get into a Halloween party at a hotel in Jacksonville, according to police. Investigators believe the girl and two adults who were shot were innocent bystanders caught in the crossfire after an argument escalated into gunfire, according to police. Another shooting in Jacksonville erupted hours later outside a Halloween house party that left a 20-year-old man dead and nine others, including a 15-year-old girl, injured, police said. No arrests have been made in either shooting. 1 killed, 8 wounded near Wesleyan University in Bloomington, Illinois A 19-year-old woman was killed early Sunday when a shooting broke out at a Halloween party near the Wesleyan University campus in Bloomington, Illinois, according to police. The shooting erupted around 1:23 a.m. on East Division Street and left other people wounded, according to police. Officers were several blocks away patrolling the area when they heard gunshots, officials said. The wounded victims included individuals affiliated with Wesleyan University and Illinois State University, police said. No arrests were immediately announced. 7 injured in shooting near Indiana University on Halloween Seven people, ranging in age from 17 to 27, were wounded when gunfire broke out early Sunday morning near Indiana University in Bloomington, Indiana, police said. "None of the injured individuals are believed to be students at Indiana University, and those that provided statements to detectives stated they had come to Bloomington to party and celebrate Halloween," Bloomington Deputy Police Chief Ryan Pedigo told reporters. Pedigo said one gun was found at the scene of the shooting and a person was taken into custody. No charges have been announced. Bloomington Mayor Kerry Thomson said in a video statement on Sunday that all seven victims were in stable condition and that police had arrested a suspect. "Gun violence has visited a Bloomington celebration once again and we should all be angry. I know I am," Thompson said. 3 juveniles among 4 shot at Nashville Halloween street party Four people, including three juveniles, were shot around 12:25 a.m. local time on Sunday during a Halloween street party in Nashville, Tennessee, according to the Nashville Police Department. One of the victims was a 16-year-old girl, who was critically injured, police said. A 14-year-old boy and a 15-year-old boy, along with an 18-year-old male, were also shot in the incident, police said. Police said some of the shots were fired from a passing vehicle. No arrests were announced. University of Colorado student killed in shooting at Halloween party In Boulder, Colorado, two students from the University of Colorado were shot, one fatally, at a Halloween house party on Saturday in an area known as The Hill near the university, according to the Boulder Police Department. The University of Colorado Boulder announced Monday evening that the student who was shot and killed on Saturday was 19-year-old Luca Hanlon, a second-year media production student. On Monday, Boulder police said 18-year-old Omar Perez of Thornton, Colorado, was arrested on Monday morning and charged with first-degree murder with extreme indifference and assault in the first-degree with extreme indifference. This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/US/halloween-shootings-nation-left-17-people-dead-86/story?id=137765951

item.title: 2 people dead, hundreds rescued amid severe flooding in Florida
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Two people were killed -- one of whom died in a vehicle -- and hundreds of others were rescued since Sunday as a storm brought severe flooding in Palm Bay, Florida, according to Palm Bay Mayor Rob Medina. The deceased victims have been identified by Florida officials as Joshua Bennett, 34, and Archie Richards, 78 Emergency crews rescued hundreds of people from flooded areas using boats and special high-water vehicles, Medina said in a press conference Tuesday. Port St. Lucie Police Department - PHOTO: In this screen grab from a video posted to social media, a truck travels through flood waters in Port St. Lucie, Fla., on Nov. 3, 2026. Greg Lovett/USA Today Network via Reuters - PHOTO: Workers from A1 Moving move a voting machine out of Magnolia Park Town Hall polling precinct after flooding in the parking lot forced them to move to another location during the US midterm election in Magnolia Park, Fla., on Nov. 3, 2026. Some homes suffered major damage. One family reported that 38 inches of water had filled their living room, Medina told reporters. "That is devastation within our city," Medina said. Officials warned that flooding could continue even after the rain stops because water may take several days to drain. They urged residents to stay away from flooded roads, fast-moving water and downed power lines. Election 2026 live updates: Americans cast their votes Florida Fish & Wildlife - PHOTO: FWC officers have deployed to St. Lucie County to conduct rescue operations and assist residents affected by this week’s historic rainfall and flooding. Flooding has also affected other parts of Florida, including St. Lucie, Martin and Palm Beach counties. State officials said they are working with local leaders to determine how much damage the storm caused. A low-pressure system over the Gulf led to continuous onshore flow over the Florida peninsula on Sunday and Monday. ABC News - PHOTO: flash flood threat map Up to 2 feet of rain fell in southern Brevard County on Sunday and Monday, leading to catastrophic flooding of streets, homes and businesses. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission says it rescued more than 60 people in Brevard County on Monday. Orange County Sheriff's Office, Florida - PHOTO: After heavy rain caused flash flooding across Brevard County, OCSO’s High Water Rescue Team deployed to the Melbourne area on Nov. 2, 2026, working into the early morning hours to rescue trapped residents. New York state reports 1st measles-associated death in over 30 years Area schools have been closed and polling stations have been relocated, according to officials. Persistent onshore flow will keep scattered showers along Florida's east coast on Tuesday, with additional rainfall of 1 to 2 inches, with locally 3 to 5 inches or more, possible. Tina Gamez-Elieson - PHOTO: In this screen grab from a video taken on Nov. 2, 2026, a student released off the school bus walks in thigh-deep flood waters in Port St Lucie, Fla. Florida Lt. Gov. Jay Collins visited Palm Bay to see the damage and meet with families affected by the flooding. He thanked first responders and residents who helped their neighbors during the emergency. "This is heartbreaking. When you talk to citizens who literally just moved here, from Louisiana, got set up, got settled — everything they own is wrecked. It’s a huge loss," Collins said.
